answer: Every epoch the beacon takes the network's pulse and draws a random grove of seven auditors to inspect one newcomer each — the fake never knows which grove, or when. A single audit demands a full trace of real work: one fake must survive four audits before it earns, each audit costing an epoch of genuine effort that cannot be copied to the next fake. One failed audit exposes the shared vine tying the batch together, and the whole batch is cut at once. An honest agent passes its one audit and is done; a farm of 1,000 fakes owes 4,000 audits of real work.
